deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no computation. It is a German prose draft about how to define the connectivity (Zusammenhang) of a surface. It is almost certainly a draft remark or footnote connected with the 1857 Crelle paper 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'. The following page is a draft letter to the editor (Borchardt) about additions to the Abelian-functions memoir, 'Figur zur Veranschaulichung' and proofs.

Content in modern terms:

(1) Cross-cut definition. A surface T is called (n+1)-fold connected if n cross-cuts (Querschnitte) cut it into a simply connected surface. A cross-cut is an arc running from boundary to boundary. Riemann notes this is the definition he used in his Dissertation (1851). With this definition one must prove that the number is well defined: if one system of n cross-cuts makes T simply connected, then every other system of cross-cuts that does so also has n members. In modern terms the cross-cut number is a topological invariant. For a compact bordered surface it equals 2 - chi(T), equivalently 2p + b - 1 for genus p and b boundary components (my addition).

(2) Comparison with the definition 'in der vorstehenden Abhandlung'. That is the 1857 paper, 'Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs'. There T is (n+1)-fold connected if one can draw n closed curves a_1, ..., a_n that neither singly nor jointly bound a part of T, while together with them every closed curve bounds. This is a homology-type definition: the rank of H_1(T) is n.

(3) Riemann's verdict. The cross-cut definition has greater intuitiveness (Anschaulichkeit). He nevertheless preferred the curve definition, for three reasons:
- the study of periodicity leads to it directly (periods of integrals of exact differentials depend only on the homology class of the closed path);
- the proofs become simpler;
- the approach carries over easily to multiply extended continuous manifolds (mehrfach ausgedehnte Mannigfaltigkeiten, i.e. higher-dimensional connectivity numbers).
The page breaks off in a heavily corrected sentence.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page states definitions and a methodological preference, not derivations.

The remark that the cross-cut definition requires an invariance proof is correct and is exactly the gap Riemann addresses in the 1857 paper; his own proofs there were later judged not fully rigorous by modern standards (rigorous treatments: e.g. Weyl 1913).

results.what: Definition of (n+1)-fold connected surface via n cross-cuts reducing it to a simply connected one, with the required invariance of n
results.modern_name: Connectivity number / first Betti number of a bordered surface (2 - Euler characteristic)

results.what: Alternative definition via maximal systems of non-bounding closed curves (homology rank), preferred because periodicity of integrals leads to it
results.modern_name: Rank of first homology group H_1

results.what: Remark that the curve/homology definition generalizes to multiply extended manifolds
results.usually_credited_to: Betti 1871 (inspired by Riemann's posthumous 'Fragment aus der Analysis Situs'), Poincaré

deep.surprise_reason: The material is known Riemann content: both definitions and the generalization to higher-dimensional manifolds are attested in his 1851 and 1857 publications and the posthumous analysis-situs fragment. The draft adds a mild historical detail: Riemann's explicit motives for preferring the homological definition over the cross-cut one, in a remark tied to correspondence with the editor.

checkable.asserts: Cross-cut connectivity number 2 - chi equals 2p + b - 1 for a surface of genus p with b boundary circles
A closed Riemann surface of genus p with one puncture/boundary is (2p+1)-fold connected, i.e. needs 2p cross-cuts, matching Riemann's 1857 count
Disk is simply connected (connectivity 1), annulus is doubly connected (connectivity 2)

transcription_corrections: The marginal insertion at top right ('jedes mögliche [?]') is doubtful; the image suggests something like 'für mich geschickter' or a similar phrase. In any case the definition needs only the existence of n cross-cuts, with invariance proved afterwards.
'die Schule [?]' inserted above 'Diese Definition' is unreliable; possibly 'die übliche'.
'Zahligkeit [?]' after 'Periodicität' is uncertain; the reading is unclear, possibly a word referring to integrals, the multi-valuedness of functions, or 'Integrale'.
'vielfach gegliederter stetiger Mannigfaltigkeit' is most likely 'mehrfach ausgedehnter stetiger Mannigfaltigkeiten', Riemann's standard term.
The final line probably reads 'und sich diese Behandlungsweise leicht auf ... ausdehnen läßt'; there is a separate marginal note at right ('und deshalb [?] ...').
